name: tractor_front
source: Plausible Magic Formula coefficients for a radial agricultural front tyre (e.g. 480/65R24 class), following Pacejka 'Tyre and Vehicle Dynamics' 3rd ed. ch. 4's MF5.2 structure. Peak friction on a firm/paved surface (Dx1/Dy1 ~= 0.85) and higher rolling resistance/lower stiffness than a passenger radial reflect the general agricultural-tyre trends reported in Wong, 'Theory of Ground Vehicles', 5th ed., ch. 1 (Table 1.3) and ch. 2 - not a measured/proprietary .tir. unloaded_radius=0.8 m matches data/models/tractor/tractor.rig.json's front wheel radius. PHYS-036 (2026-09-24): same 'aligning' sign/shape fix as data/tyres/passenger_car_225_45r17.json - qdz1/qdz2 flipped (was +0.11/-0.02) so Mz0 = -t*Fy0 (Pacejka's own convention, Dz opposite sign to Dy) instead of reinforcing Fy0; qbz1 raised from 6.0 to 52.8 (same B-scaling technique, shape unchanged) so the curve peaks at ~4.5 deg of slip (a larger, softer ag tyre's trail is expected to fall off a little later than a stiffer passenger tyre's ~4 deg, still well inside the qualitative 2-6 deg range Milliken ch. 2 and Wong ch. 2 describe) instead of the un-fixed curve's ~39.6 deg.
